reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about confinement-controlled nucleation, diffusion suppression, and alloy homogeneity, but no cited evidence is provided to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific mechanistic link between mesoporous confinement and simultaneous nucleation of five noble metals under thermal shock, so the lack of supporting passages leaves all key premises ungrounded.
premises: Geometric confinement within mesoporous supports can restrict atomic diffusion during nucleation
Restricted diffusion forces nearly simultaneous nucleation of diverse metal species
Simultaneous nucleation in a confined volume enforces homogeneous alloy formation and prevents phase segregation
Rapid thermal shock to ~923 K can decompose precursors and initiate nucleation within the confined pores
The outcome depends on pore size: smaller, well-characterized pores provide effective confinement; larger or less controlled pores do not
